claim_text: A server can authorize credentialed cross-origin requests from any origin by returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
evidence_text: When a response to a credentialed request has Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to true, the Access-Control-Allow-Origin value must identify the requesting origin; the wildcard value is not permitted for this response.
verification_rationale: The evidence says that a credentialed response must specify the requesting origin and cannot use the wildcard value. It therefore contradicts the claim that the wildcard can authorize credentialed requests from any origin.
